page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This instance includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. It does not include any GPU accelerators. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching a top-tier 36.47 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving a strong 15.05 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded scaling and memory write bandwidth show relative weaknesses, with stress-ng multi-core performance and large-block memory write bandwidth falling into the lower percentiles. Passmark CPU, database operations, and Redis SET operations consistently perform in the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ds_v7 offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that benefit from high single-core clock speeds and local NVMe storage without requiring massive multi-threaded scaling. It is well-suited for applications such as lightweight database hosting, static web serving, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from 2 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores running at 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, a 480 MB L3 cache, and 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. Benchmarks reveal exceptional single-threaded performance, highlighted by top-tier gzip compression and strong bzip3 decompression, though multi-threaded scaling and memory write bandwidth are relatively weak. Overall, Passmark CPU, database operations, and Redis SET benchmarks demonstrate solid average performance. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and lightweight database applications that leverage high single-core speeds and local high-speed storage.
